reading: The 7x7 input is noise dominated by one colour (1, 2 or 3); the output is a fixed 3x3 colour-8 pattern chosen by that dominant colour (1 -> 008/880/080, 2 -> 000/888/000, 3 -> 088/080/080).

slots.feature: most frequent non-background colour of the input
slots.lookup: learned table dominant colour -> fixed 3x3 pattern of 8 on 0 (from train)

why: pairs with the same dominant colour have identical outputs; output is always 3x3

reading: Each isolated marker cell is surrounded by a 3x3 ring; the ring colour depends on the marker colour (3 -> 6, 8 -> 4, 2 -> 1). The marker itself stays.
why: every marker's 8 neighbours take the mapped colour; nothing else changes
invariants: all cells not adjacent to a marker

reading: The 3x3 input is copied N times (N = number of non-background cells) into an output of B x B blocks (B = number of background cells), filling blocks in reading order; remaining blocks stay empty.
why: every 3x3 block is the input or empty; count of copies = fg cell count, blocks per side = bg cell count
invariants: each copy identical to the input

reading: Each input cell is scaled up into a 3x3 block of its colour (3x upscale).

slots.unit: each input cell becomes a factor x factor block

why: output size is 3x input size and each 3x3 block is uniform with the colour of the corresponding input cell

reading: Four grey(5) marker cells lie above, below, left and right of a hollow shape; a rectangle outline in the shape's colour is drawn one cell inside the markers' bounding box.

slots.bounds: box spanned by the four 5-markers, inset by one cell on each side

why: the new outline is exactly the perimeter of the inset marker box; markers and the shape stay unchanged

reading: Separator lines cut the grid into equal cells; one cell holds a pattern. The pattern is copied into every cell whose row index and column index differ from the source cell's by an even number (every second cell in both directions).

slots.anchors: panels at even row/column panel-offsets from the source panel

why: every panel with same parity as the source equals the source; all other panels stay empty; separators unchanged

reading: The top row is a colour legend; around the single marker below the separator, concentric square rings are drawn, ring at Chebyshev distance r taking legend colour r (r=0 is the centre), clipped at the grid edge.

slots.centre: the single non-background cell below the separator
slots.palette: legend row 0, read left to right up to the last non-zero entry
slots.rings: cell at Chebyshev distance r gets palette[r]

why: every cell within the legend length of the marker has the legend colour of its ring distance; legend and separator unchanged (pair 0 output also shows legend cell 5 turned from 8 to 5, unexplained)

reading: A 2x2 block of four colours sits in the grid; at each of its four diagonal corners a 2x2 block is placed (clipped at edges) coloured with the colour of the diagonally opposite cell of the block.

slots.subject: the 2x2 four-colour block
slots.anchors: the four diagonal-outside 2x2 positions adjacent to the block's corners
slots.colour: colour of the block cell diagonally opposite to that corner

why: each outside 2x2 corner block is uniform with the opposite block colour; the original block unchanged

reading: Frames are marked by four L-shaped corner brackets; the colour-1 pattern inside each frame is completed by mirroring it across the frame's midline along its long side (union with its reflection), and stray colour-1 cells outside all frames are erased.

slots.region: interior of each bracket frame (box between the four corner brackets)
slots.axis: midline perpendicular to the frame's long side
slots.subject: colour-1 cells inside the frame

why: inside each frame the 1-pattern is symmetric about the frame's midline and contains the input pattern; no 1 cells remain outside frames

reading: Full grey separator lines cut the grid into cells; the top-left cell is filled with 1, the centre cell (middle row band, middle column band) with 2, and the bottom-right cell with 3.

slots.regions: panels cut by separators: first (top-left), centre (middle band in both directions), last (bottom-right)

why: exactly those three panels are filled solid with their colours; separators and other panels unchanged
